newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Kuehbacher doubts Bonn can meet EMU goal.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Kuehbacher doubts Bonn can meet EMU goal.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said in remarks published Tuesday he doubts that Germany can meet Maastricht Treaty deficit criteria and that failing to do so would leave Bonn with only one option -- to delay the start of monetary union.

In an interview with with the Boerse Online magazine released to the media today, Kuehbacher said of Germany's ability to reduce its budget deficit to the Maastricht Treaty mandated three percent level, "in view of the current economic developments I have my doubts."
The magazine said the interview was published last Wednesday and will go on news stands tomorrow.

Kuehbacher said, "If I interpret the criteria verbatim, as Finance Minister Theo Waigel has always demanded, and if I look at the ruling of the Constitutional Court, delay is the only consequence, unless the Federal government still manages to limit the deficit to three percent of GDP."

Asked if a delay in monetary union was the only option since tax increases would hurt the economy, Kuehbacher said, "Yes," adding that that when tax revenues estimates are made in May that the "government will no longer be able to shirk the decision on whether to delay EMU."

Koehbacher said that given recent comments from German government officials that fulfiling the criteria is more important than the planned 1999 EMU launch date that "one can do nothing other than decide as quickly as possible on the delay."
Kuehbacher added that for the government to reach the Maastricht deficit target of three percent that budget measures totalling 15 billion marks are needed.
